as_told.title: CIA Office of Global Access, JSOC and NEST in crash retrievals

plain: A little-known CIA office called the Office of Global Access is said to be the main part of a worldwide program that recovers crashed UFOs. Michels tells it many times, saying the story came from reporting in the Daily Mail, a British newspaper. In his words, the office is "the main you know part of the crash retrieval program all around the world." A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb credits the journalist Christopher Sharp with breaking the story. He says the office "was created under the DS&T in the year 2003", meaning the CIA's science and technology branch. Michels names a man called Doug Wolf as linked to the office, which he says did "rapid response" retrievals "all over the world" in the early 2000s. In one telling he adds, without citing the paper, that it is "rumored to coordinate closely" with the military's top special forces command and with teams that respond to nuclear emergencies. If true, it would mean the CIA has a standing team for collecting crashed craft around the globe.
